risk: Public attack surface. Any authorization, injection or abuse flaw is reachable by anyone; no gateway/WAF layer to absorb it.
control: API gateway + WAF in front; OIDC authN; object-level authZ; schema validation; origin reachable only from gateway.

risk: No attribution, no per-person revocation, one leaked credential gives full cloud control. Defeats every other fix.
control: Named admin identities via SSO; JIT elevation (PAM); sealed break-glass; disable shared account and its keys.

risk: Phishing, credential stuffing or infostealer logs give direct access to cloud, Git, CI and admin UI.
control: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/passkey) for admins; MFA for all staff on IdP, cloud, Git, CI, VPN, admin UI.

risk: Laptop theft, malware or a synced backup exposes production access. Keys are also likely in shell history and dotfiles.
control: Rotate all; move to secrets manager; workload identity for services; disk encryption + EDR on laptops.

risk: Force multiplier: after any app compromise, root makes container escape and host tampering easier.
control: Non-root USER, drop capabilities, read-only rootfs, seccomp default; admission policy to enforce.

risk: Python/AI stacks pull large transitive dependency trees; known-vulnerable packages ship unnoticed.
control: SCA (pip-audit/OSV), image scan (Trivy/Grype), SBOM in CI; report-only day 1, gate criticals by day 30.

finding: Prod DB reachable from developer IPs
risk: Patient data store exposed to the least-controlled endpoints. Stolen laptop or dev credential reaches PHI directly.
control: Remove IP allow-rules; private subnet only; JIT read-only access through audited DB proxy (Part 5).

risk: PHI copied into a broadly readable log store: a live PDPL exposure today, independent of any attacker.
control: Stop body/prompt logging; redact at source; restrict then purge existing logs (after legal-hold check).

risk: PHI may leave the Kingdom to a third party with unknown retention, training and residency terms.
control: Interim gate: no PHI to external LLM. Egress proxy with redaction/tokenization; provider due diligence + DPA.

risk: Unknown recoverability. Ransomware, operator error or corruption becomes an unbounded outage and data-loss event.
control: Restore test into isolated env with measured RTO/RPO; immutable, encrypted, separate-account copies; monthly test.

risk: Detection blindness and slow investigations; attacker dwell time grows; cannot answer regulators or customers.
control: Central pipeline for cloud audit, IdP, gateway, app auth/audit into one SIEM; NTP; retention policy.

risk: Scraping, credential stuffing and LLM cost exhaustion (denial-of-wallet) with no brake.
control: Gateway rate limits + quotas per user/tenant/key; LLM token budgets; bulk-export caps.

risk: Highest-privilege application function exposed to brute force, phishing and any auth-bypass bug.
control: Move behind ZTNA/VPN + SSO + step-up MFA; separate admin host; IP allow-list as interim.

risk: Retrieval without per-user authorization leaks other users'/tenants' documents; poisoned documents steer the model.
control: Authorization-aware retrieval (tenant + ACL pre-filter, policy re-check); untrusted-content handling; canary tests.

risk: A prompt-injected agent inherits broad power: data theft, record changes, account creation.
control: Per-agent identity; per-tool scoped short-lived on-behalf-of tokens; tool gateway; disable write tools first.

risk: A leaked pipeline secret allows attacker-controlled deployments and supply-chain compromise.
control: OIDC federation to short-lived, environment-scoped roles; remove static keys; rotate now.

risk: Not a breach path itself; causes drift, ad-hoc decisions and unanswerable customer questions.
control: Approve risk-based SLA and exception process (Part 8); weekly aging report.

risk: First incident is improvised: slow containment, missed notification deadlines, lost evidence.
control: v1 IR plan, on-call, contacts, severity matrix, customer/regulator decision tree; tabletop.

risk: Cannot protect, patch or scope what is not known; shadow assets and orphaned keys persist.
control: Auto-generated inventory from cloud APIs, repos and registry; mandatory owner and data-class tags.
